# Introduction

[STING](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stimulator_of_interferon_genes)-associated vasculopathy with onset in infancy (**SAVI**) is caused by gain-of-function mutations in *STING1*. De Cevins *et al.* performed single-cell RNA-seq of PBMCs from SAVI patients and healthy controls, and an IFN-β time-course in healthy PBMCs, to dissect IFN-dependent and IFN-independent programmes. They highlight disease-associated monocytes and propose a **21-gene** transcriptomic signature of STING activation that is **enriched for TNF-α / NF-κB–related biology** and **filtered against IFN-β–induced genes** in monocytes and DCs (Figure 6; Table S6).

**Primary publication (open access):** de Cevins, C., *et al.* (2023). Single-cell RNA-sequencing of PBMCs from SAVI patients reveals disease-associated monocytes with elevated integrated stress response. *Cell Reports Medicine* **4**, 101333. <https://doi.org/10.1016/j.xcrm.2023.101333> — PMC: <https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10772457/>.

**Data:** scRNA-seq are deposited under superseries [GSE226601](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE226601): SAVI cohort [GSE226598](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE226598), IFN-β dataset [GSE226572](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE226572). Pseudobulk for this notebook is prepared in `dev/SAVI/data/prepare_data.R` from the GEO Seurat object.

**Scope of this document:** We do **not** reproduce the paper’s within-study differential analysis or IFN-β filtering steps here. We use their **published 21-gene symbol list** (Table S6 / Figure 6) as biomarkers, fit or load **monocytic-lineage** reference models from the lab `targets` store, and attach **SAVI sample × cell type** pseudobulk plus **`offset == 0`** reference samples for planned comparisons to healthy baselines (same structural role as `pam50_toy_model.qmd` for breast cancer).

# STING activation signature (21 genes)

The symbols below follow **Table S6** / Figure 6 in de Cevins *et al.* (2023). We map HGNC symbols to Ensembl via `org.Hs.eg.db` for overlap with the reference model feature space; **lncRNAs and some readthrough ids** may return `NA` here even when present in the single-cell count matrix — those rows are dropped from the `targets`-based extraction unless you supply Ensembl ids manually.

```{r}
#| label: sting-signature
sting_signature_21 <- tibble(
  gene = c(
    "AC253572.2",
    "ADRB2",
    "ANKRD28",
    "ANXA1",
    "AQP9",
    "AZIN1-AS1",
    "IL1B",
    "JARID2",
    "KLF4",
    "MIR4435-2HG",
    "OTUD1",
    "PLAUR",
    "PTGS2",
    "PTX3",
    "SELENOK",
    "TGIF1",
    "TREM1",
    "TSC22D2",
    "ZBTB43",
    "ZFP36L2",
    "ZNF503"
  )
) |>
  mutate(
    .feature = AnnotationDbi::mapIds(
      org.Hs.eg.db::org.Hs.eg.db,
      keys = gene,
      column = "ENSEMBL",
      keytype = "SYMBOL",
      multiVals = "first"
    )
  )

sting_signature_21
```

# Reference model store (`targets`)

Posterior HCA models live under `params$model_store_root`, in a subfolder named after the harmonised cell type (here `V1_monocytic` when `params$target_cell_type` is `"monocytic"`). Branch metadata encodes which Ensembl gene each `estimates_chunk_*` target belongs to (`Gene:___ENSG...___` in the recorded warning field).

```{r}
#| label: model-meta
model_path <- file.path(
  params$model_store_root,
  paste0("V1_", params$target_cell_type)
)

model_meta <-
  targets::tar_meta(
    starts_with("estimates_chunk_"),
    store = file.path(model_path, "_targets")
  ) |>
  dplyr::filter(type == "branch") |>
  mutate(
    .feature = stringr::str_extract(
      warnings,
      "(?<=Gene:___)ENSG\\d+(?=___)"
    )
  )

# How many of the 21 (with successful SYMBOL→ENSEMBL map) appear in the store?
n_sig_in_store <- sum(sting_signature_21$.feature %in% model_meta$.feature, na.rm = TRUE)
n_sig_mapped <- sum(!is.na(sting_signature_21$.feature))

tibble(
  signature_genes = nrow(sting_signature_21),
  mapped_to_ensembl = n_sig_mapped,
  present_in_targets_store = n_sig_in_store
)
```

# Fit and compress `brms` models (optional, heavy)

Set **`params$run_fits: true`** when rendering (or in the YAML) to re-run extraction, posterior correlation partitioning, `poco::compress_brmsfit`, and `saveRDS`. By default this chunk is **skipped** and the next section loads `params$estimates_rds`.

For each gene: read the precomputed `estimates_chunk` from disk (`tar_read_raw()` from the **targets** package, same usage as `dev/posteriorHCA_brms_fit_compression_test.qmd`), strip large environments from the fit, optionally compress with `poco`, and record layout / fidelity metrics.

```{r}
#| label: fit-sting-biomarkers
#| eval: !expr params$run_fits

handlers(global = TRUE)
handlers("progress")

options(future.globals.maxSize = 5 * 1024^3)

n_components <- params$n_components
corr_threshold <- params$corr_threshold

extract_one_biomarker <- function(ensg) {
  estimates_chunk <-
    model_meta |>
    dplyr::filter(.feature == ensg) |>
    dplyr::pull(name) |>
    tar_read_raw(store = file.path(model_path, "_targets")) |>
    dplyr::select(-tar_group) |>
    mutate(
      gene = sting_signature_21 |>
        dplyr::filter(!is.na(.feature), .feature == ensg) |>
        dplyr::pull(gene),
      cell_type = params$target_cell_type,
      brms_fit = purrr::map(brms_fit, poco::strip_brmsfit_envs)
    )

  fit_brms <- estimates_chunk$brms_fit[[1]]

  posterior_cor <- poco::posterior_correlation(
    fit_brms,
    type = "correlation",
    method = "pearson"
  )
  original_draws <- posterior::as_draws_matrix(fit_brms)

  partition <- poco::partition_parameters_clusters(
    posterior_cor,
    threshold = corr_threshold,
    min_size = 2L,
    simple_output = FALSE
  )

  layout_tbl <- tibble(
    n_components = n_components,
    corr_threshold = corr_threshold,
    n_blocks = length(partition$blocks),
    block_size_max = if (length(partition$blocks)) max(lengths(partition$blocks)) else 0L,
    block_size_med = if (length(partition$blocks)) {
      as.integer(stats::median(lengths(partition$blocks)))
    } else {
      0L
    },
    n_remainder = length(partition$remainder)
  )

  compress_tic <- Sys.time()
  compressed_blockwise <- tryCatch(
    poco::compress_brmsfit(
      brmsfit = fit_brms,
      method = "mclust",
      n_components = n_components,
      partition = partition,
      cluster_BPPARAM = 1L,
      verbose = FALSE
    ),
    error = function(e) {
      warning(
        "compress_brmsfit failed: ",
        conditionMessage(e),
        call. = FALSE,
        immediate. = TRUE
      )
      NULL
    }
  )
  time_used <- as.numeric(difftime(Sys.time(), compress_tic, units = "secs"))

  fid_blockwise <- if (is.null(compressed_blockwise)) {
    NULL
  } else {
    tryCatch(
      poco::evaluate_compression(
        compressed_blockwise$compressed,
        original_draws,
        seed = 1L
      ),
      error = function(e) {
        warning(
          "evaluate_compression failed: ",
          conditionMessage(e),
          call. = FALSE,
          immediate. = TRUE
        )
        NULL
      }
    )
  }

  if (is.null(compressed_blockwise)) {
    layout_tbl <- layout_tbl |>
      mutate(
        compression_ok = FALSE,
        time_used = NA_real_,
        compression_rate = NA_real_,
        energy_pct = NA_real_,
        c2st_pct = NA_real_,
        reproduction_pct = NA_real_
      )
  } else {
    estimates_chunk$brms_fit_compressed <- list(compressed_blockwise)
    layout_tbl <- layout_tbl |>
      mutate(
        compression_ok = TRUE,
        time_used = time_used,
        compression_rate =
          as.numeric(lobstr::obj_size(compressed_blockwise)) /
            as.numeric(lobstr::obj_size(fit_brms))
      )
  }

  if (is.null(fid_blockwise)) {
    layout_tbl <- layout_tbl |>
      mutate(
        energy_pct = NA_real_,
        c2st_pct = NA_real_,
        reproduction_pct = NA_real_
      )
  } else {
    en <- fid_blockwise$metrics$energy$reproduction_pct
    c2 <- fid_blockwise$metrics$c2st$reproduction_pct
    layout_tbl <- layout_tbl |>
      mutate(
        energy_pct = if (is.null(en)) NA_real_ else en,
        c2st_pct = if (is.null(c2)) NA_real_ else c2,
        reproduction_pct = fid_blockwise$reproduction_pct
      )
  }

  estimates_chunk |> tibble::add_column(layout_tbl)
}

sting_signature_21 |>
  dplyr::filter(.feature %in% model_meta$.feature) |>
  dplyr::pull(.feature) -> biomarkers

with_progress({
  p <- progressr::progressor(along = biomarkers)
  sting_estimates_chunk <- purrr::map_dfr(biomarkers, function(ensg) {
    p(sprintf("Processing %s", ensg))
    extract_one_biomarker(ensg)
  })
})

saveRDS(sting_estimates_chunk, params$estimates_rds)
```

# SAVI pseudobulk and healthy reference samples

**SAVI object:** RDS produced by `prepare_data.R` — pseudobulk counts aggregated with Seurat `AggregateExpression` by **`Sample`** and **`CellType`** (see GEO object metadata for treatment and category).

**Reference:** `pseudobulk_sample` from the same monocytic `targets` store is a `SummarizedExperiment` whose count assay is backed by the shared **Zenodo `pseudobulk_se.h5ad`** path. Rows with **`offset == 0`** are interpreted as healthy baseline samples for merge and posterior comparison (analogous to the breast epithelial reference in `pam50_toy_model.qmd`).

**Merge (same idea as `pam50_toy_model.qmd` § merge-se):** `SAVI_pseudobulk_sobj` is a **Seurat** object whose **RNA assay counts are row-named by gene symbol**. We map symbols → **Ensembl** (deduplicated), build a `SummarizedExperiment` with **`sample_role = "savi_pseudobulk"`**, then **column-bind** with reference columns after intersecting **shared Ensembl ids** and **assay names**.

```{r}
#| label: merge-savi-reference


SAVI_pseudobulk_sobj <- 
  readRDS(params$savi_pseudobulk_rds) %>% 
  filter(CellType == '17. Disease-associated monocytes')

pseudobulk_sample <- targets::tar_read(
  pseudobulk_sample,
  store = file.path(model_path, "_targets")
)

# Point DelayedArray/HDF5 backend to the local h5ad-backed matrix (path may differ on HPC)
pseudobulk_sample@assays@data@listData[["counts"]]@seed@seed@seed@filepath <-
  params$pseudobulk_h5ad

ref_sample <-
  pseudobulk_sample |>
  dplyr::filter(offset == 0)

SummarizedExperiment::colData(ref_sample)$sample_role <- "reference"

# --- SAVI: Seurat counts are rownames = gene symbols (see prepare_data.R) ---
counts_sym <- as.matrix(
  tryCatch(
    SeuratObject::LayerData(SAVI_pseudobulk_sobj, assay = "RNA", layer = "counts"),
    error = function(e) {
      Seurat::GetAssayData(SAVI_pseudobulk_sobj, assay = "RNA", slot = "counts")
    }
  )
)

sym <- rownames(counts_sym)
ensg <- AnnotationDbi::mapIds(
  org.Hs.eg.db::org.Hs.eg.db,
  keys = sym,
  column = "ENSEMBL",
  keytype = "SYMBOL",
  multiVals = "first"
)
keep <- !is.na(ensg) & !duplicated(ensg)
ensg <- ensg[keep]

counts_ens <- counts_sym[keep, , drop = FALSE]
rownames(counts_ens) <- ensg

cd_savi <- as.data.frame(SAVI_pseudobulk_sobj@meta.data)
rownames(cd_savi) <- colnames(counts_ens)
cd_savi$sample_role <- "savi_pseudobulk"
cd_savi$offset <- 0L
if (!"cell_type_unified_ensemble" %in% names(cd_savi)) {
  cd_savi$cell_type_unified_ensemble <- cd_savi$CellType
}

se_savi_ensembl <- SummarizedExperiment::SummarizedExperiment(
  assays = list(counts = counts_ens),
  colData = S4Vectors::DataFrame(cd_savi, row.names = colnames(counts_ens)),
  rowData = S4Vectors::DataFrame(
    gene_symbol = sym[keep],
    row.names = ensg
  )
)

# --- rbind-like merge of SE columns (intersect genes, union colData columns) ---
merge_summarized_experiments <- function(...) {
  ses <- list(...)
  assay_names <- Reduce(intersect, lapply(ses, SummarizedExperiment::assayNames))
  if (length(assay_names) == 0L) {
    stop("No shared assays between SummarizedExperiment objects.")
  }

  genes <- Reduce(intersect, lapply(ses, rownames))
  if (length(genes) == 0L) {
    stop("No shared rownames between SummarizedExperiment objects.")
  }

  ses <- lapply(ses, function(se) se[genes, , drop = FALSE])

  cds <- lapply(ses, function(se) as.data.frame(SummarizedExperiment::colData(se)))
  all_nms <- Reduce(union, lapply(cds, names))
  cds <- lapply(cds, function(cd) {
    missing <- setdiff(all_nms, names(cd))
    for (nm in missing) cd[[nm]] <- NA
    cd[, all_nms, drop = FALSE]
  })

  # Dense coercion: SAVI counts are an ordinary matrix; reference counts are often
  # HDF5Array/DelayedArray. Mixed cbind() hits bindCOLS() with no suitable method.
  assays <- stats::setNames(
    lapply(assay_names, function(an) {
      mats <- lapply(ses, function(se) {
        base::as.matrix(SummarizedExperiment::assay(se, an))
      })
      do.call(base::cbind, mats)
    }),
    assay_names
  )

  SummarizedExperiment::SummarizedExperiment(
    assays = assays,
    colData = S4Vectors::DataFrame(
      do.call(rbind, cds),
      row.names = unlist(lapply(ses, colnames), use.names = FALSE)
    ),
    rowData = SummarizedExperiment::rowData(ses[[1]])
  )
}

se_monocytic <- merge_summarized_experiments(
  se_savi_ensembl,
  ref_sample
)

# Copy abundance flag from reference rowData when a single .abundant* column exists
rd_ref <- as.data.frame(SummarizedExperiment::rowData(ref_sample))
abundant_cols <- grep("^\\.abundant", names(rd_ref), value = TRUE)
if (length(abundant_cols) >= 1L) {
  ac <- abundant_cols[[1]]
  SummarizedExperiment::rowData(se_monocytic)$.abundant <-
    SummarizedExperiment::rowData(ref_sample)[rownames(se_monocytic), ac, drop = TRUE]
}

tibble::tibble(
  n_features = nrow(se_monocytic),
  n_samples = ncol(se_monocytic),
  n_savi = sum(SummarizedExperiment::colData(se_monocytic)$sample_role == "savi_pseudobulk"),
  n_reference = sum(SummarizedExperiment::colData(se_monocytic)$sample_role == "reference")
)
```

```{r}
#| label: scale-abundance
ref_sample_name <-
  se_monocytic %>%
  colData() %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  filter(sample_role == "reference") %>%
  rownames()

se_monocytic <-
  se_monocytic %>%
  tidybulk::scale_abundance(
    method = "TMMwsp",
    reference_sample = ref_sample_name
  ) %>%
  mutate(offset = log(1 / multiplier))
```

# SAVI sample annotations (GEO [GSE226598](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE226598))

Per-sample metadata (age, sex, 10x library batch, GSM accession) is taken from the GEO **series matrix** for GSE226598 (same fields as the GEO web “Sample characteristics” table). Each GSM links to its own GEO sample page.

After `scale_abundance`, we add harmonised columns for downstream models:

- **`tissue_groups`**: `"blood"` for SAVI pseudobulk columns only (PBMC in the study).
- **`sex`**, **`age_years`**: GEO values; **C1**, **C2** (“Adult”) and **P5_STING** (“Ped”) get **imputed numeric years** (see below) so `age_decade` / models can run without `NA`.
- **`age_decade`**: `as.character(ceiling(age_years / 10))` for SAVI once **`age_years`** is set (including imputed).
- **`age_group`**: `"pediatric"` if `age_years < 18`, else `"adult"` (SAVI columns only).
- **`age_decade_model`**: same as **`age_decade`** here (decade index from imputed / observed years).
- **`age_imputed`**: `TRUE` when **`age_years`** was filled by the rule below, not present as a number in GEO.

### Interpreting GEO **“Adult”** (C1, C2) and **“Ped”** (P5)

The cohort in de Cevins *et al.* (2023) comprises **five SAVI patients** and **seven healthy controls** (Figure 1A; GEO [GSE226598](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE226598)). GEO lists **“age: Adult”** for **C1** / **C2** and **“age: Ped”** for **P5_STING** without a year.

**Imputation used in this notebook** (rounded integers, documented for reproducibility):

| Sample(s) | GEO label | Imputed `age_years` | Rationale |
|-------------|-----------|---------------------|-----------|
| **C1**, **C2** | Adult | **35** | Mean of adult controls with numeric ages in the same series (**C8** 36 y, **C9** 35 y), aligned with matched adult controls. |
| **P5_STING** | Ped | **8** | Central value among other paediatric SAVI / control ages in GEO for this series (e.g. P1 4 y, P4 7–9 y, P6 8–10 y). |

All other donors keep **GEO-reported** ages. **`age_imputed`** is `TRUE` only for **C1**, **C2**, and **P5_STING**. Replace these constants if you obtain exact ages from authors or supplements.

- **`sex`**, **`assay_groups`**, **`assay_groups___altered`**: after GEO join, values are **harmonised to the Immune Atlas / posteriorHCA vocabulary** (same as `posteriorHCA::expr_predict()` / `Introduction` vignette: **`male`**, **`female`**, **`unknown`**; assay **`10x Genomics 3`**). GEO still uses **M**/**F** and Chromium **3′ v2**/**v3** batches in the series matrix; we do not keep the long Chromium strings in `colData` because the reference model was trained on short **`assay_groups`** labels.
- **`geo_accession`**, **`geo_sample_url`**: GSM id and direct GEO sample link (same pattern as the series page [GSE226598](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE226598)).

```{r}
#| label: coldata-gse226598
# Tibble from GEO series matrix GSE226598_series_matrix.txt.gz (Sample_title,
# Sample_geo_accession, age / Sex / batch rows). Series:
# https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE226598
geo_tbl <- tibble::tribble(
  ~Sample,              ~gse_accession, ~gse_age_years, ~gse_sex, ~gse_sting_batch,
  "C10",                "GSM7079979",            10,  "M",  "STING2",
  "C11",                "GSM7079980",            16,  "M",  "STING2",
  "C1",                 "GSM7079981",            NA,  "M",  "STING3",
  "C2",                 "GSM7079982",            NA,  "M",  "STING3",
  "C7",                 "GSM7079983",             5,  "F",  "STING1",
  "C8_aunt_P1_STING",   "GSM7079984",            36,  "F",  "STING1",
  "C9_mother_P1_STING", "GSM7079985",            35,  "F",  "STING1",
  "P1_STING_ht",        "GSM7079986",             4,  "F",  "STING1",
  "P1_STING_ht_T",      "GSM7079987",             8,  "F",  "STING1",
  "P1_STING_ht_T2",     "GSM7079988",             8,  "F",  "STING1",
  "P2_STING_ht",        "GSM7079989",            31,  "M",  "STING1",
  "P2_STING_ht_T",      "GSM7079990",            34,  "M",  "STING1",
  "P4_STING_ht",        "GSM7079991",             7,  "M",  "STING2",
  "P4_STING_ht_T",      "GSM7079992",             9,  "M",  "STING2",
  "P5_STING",           "GSM7079993",            NA,  "M",  "STING3",
  "P6_STING_ht",        "GSM7079994",             8,  "M",  "STING2",
  "P6_STING_ht_T",      "GSM7079995",            10,  "M",  "STING2"
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    # Raw GEO had NA for "Adult" (C1, C2) and "Ped" (P5); impute for modelling (see prose).
    gse_age_imputed = is.na(.data$gse_age_years),
    gse_age_years = dplyr::coalesce(
      .data$gse_age_years,

    "gse_accession",
    "gse_geo_sample_url",
    "gse_age_years",
    "gse_age_imputed",
    "gse_sex"
  )
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Compare samples to healthy posterior predictive baseline

For each **STING signature gene** with a loadable compressed `brms` fit, we draw replicated counts from **`brms::posterior_predict()`** at the sample’s **`offset`** and covariates in **`colData`** (same pattern as `pam50_toy_model.qmd` § *Compare samples*). **`healthy_median`** / **`healthy_hpd_*`** summarise the predictive distribution; **`direction`** flags counts outside the central **95%** predictive mass (**two-sided** `posterior_tail_p` is for exploration only—no multiple-testing correction across genes × samples).

We use **`posterior_predict`** (not **`posterior_epred`**): we want the predictive distribution of a **new observation** including likelihood noise, because each test asks whether the observed count is in the tail of a healthy sample, not whether the latent mean differs. We also use **`re_formula = NULL`** with **`allow_new_levels = TRUE`** and **`sample_new_levels = "uncertainty"`** so that:

- `(1 + age_decade * sex + ethnicity_groups | tissue_groups)` keeps the trained **`blood`** slopes (tissue is observed).
- `(1 | dataset_id_altered)` is marginalised: a fresh dataset intercept is drawn from `N(0, sd_dataset_id_altered)` for every posterior sample — the correct "new SAVI cohort, exchangeable with the atlas" null.
- Unknown **`ethnicity_groups`** is marginalised explicitly by expanding `newdata` over all ethnicities seen in the model's training data and pooling draws (uniform mixture). Setting ethnicity to a single arbitrary value would bias the null toward that group; zeroing the term in the design matrix is not possible for a categorical fixed effect.

```{r}
#| label: gene-deviation-fn

# Categorical levels for any predictor pulled from the brms fit's training
# frame. Used to expand newdata over training-set values when a covariate is
# unknown for a test sample.
fit_levels <- function(fit, var) {
  d <- fit$data
  if (is.null(d) || !var %in% names(d)) return(character(0))
  v <- d[[var]]
  lv <- if (is.factor(v)) levels(v) else sort(unique(as.character(v)))
  lv[!is.na(lv) & nzchar(lv)]
}

# First non-NA, non-empty character among the inputs; NA_character_ otherwise.
coalesce_char <- function(...) {
  args <- list(...)
  for (v in args) {
    if (length(v) >= 1L) {
      val <- as.character(v[[1L]])
      if (!is.na(val) && nzchar(val)) return(val)
    }
  }
  NA_character_
}

# Build a single-row newdata template from colData. Columns that may be NA are
# left NA on purpose; build_newdata_grid() will marginalise over training-set
# levels when the model uses them.
newdata_for_sample <- function(se, sample_idx) {
  cd <- SummarizedExperiment::colData(se)[sample_idx, , drop = FALSE] |>
    as.data.frame()

  tibble::tibble(
    # Observed when available (may be NA -> marginalise).
    age_decade = coalesce_char(
      if ("age_decade_model" %in% names(cd)) cd$age_decade_model,
      if ("age_decade" %in% names(cd)) cd$age_decade
    ),
    sex = coalesce_char(if ("sex" %in% names(cd)) cd$sex),
    ethnicity_groups = coalesce_char(
      if ("ethnicity_groups" %in% names(cd)) cd$ethnicity_groups,
      if ("ethnicity_groups_imputed" %in% names(cd)) cd$ethnicity_groups_imputed
    ),

    # Counterfactual / required: forced to the healthy baseline so we test
    # against the atlas null, not the sample's own disease label.
    disease_groups_altered = "Normal",
    # disease_groups_altered = coalesce_char(
    #   if ("disease_groups_altered" %in% names(cd)) cd$disease_groups_altered,
    #   if ("disease_groups___altered" %in% names(cd)) cd$disease_groups___altered,
    #   "Normal"
    # ),


    # Required (atlas-defined / technical):
    assay_groups_altered = coalesce_char(
      if ("assay_groups_altered" %in% names(cd)) cd$assay_groups_altered,
      if ("assay_groups___altered" %in% names(cd)) cd$assay_groups___altered,
      if ("assay_groups" %in% names(cd)) cd$assay_groups,
      "10x Genomics 3"
    ),
    tissue_groups = coalesce_char(if ("tissue_groups" %in% names(cd)) cd$tissue_groups),
    offset = cd$offset[[1]]
  )
}

# Expand a single-row newdata into a prediction grid:
#   - required cols MUST be non-NA (e.g. tissue_groups)
#   - marginalize_over cols that are NA in newdata AND present in fit$data
#     are expanded across the training-set levels (uniform mixture)
#   - new_level_cols (e.g. dataset_id_altered) are stamped with a fresh unique
#     placeholder so brms (allow_new_levels = TRUE, sample_new_levels =
#     "uncertainty") draws a new group effect from its posterior population.
build_newdata_grid <- function(
  fit,
  newdata,
  marginalize_over = c("sex", "age_decade", "ethnicity_groups", "assay_groups_altered"),
  required = c("tissue_groups", "offset", "disease_groups_altered"),
  new_level_cols = "dataset_id_altered",
  new_level_tag = NULL
) {
  stopifnot(NROW(newdata) == 1L)
  newdata <- tibble::as_tibble(newdata)

  is_blank <- function(v) {
    length(v) == 0L ||
      is.na(v[[1L]]) ||
      (is.character(v[[1L]]) && !nzchar(v[[1L]]))
  }

  fit_vars <- colnames(fit$data)

  # Required columns must be present and non-empty.
  for (col in required) {
    if (!col %in% fit_vars) next
    if (!col %in% names(newdata) || is_blank(newdata[[col]])) {
      stop(sprintf(
        "Required predictor `%s` is missing or empty in newdata.",
        col
      ))
    }
  }

  # Decide which columns to expand.
  to_expand <- character(0)
  for (col in marginalize_over) {
    if (!col %in% fit_vars) next
    if (!col %in% names(newdata) || is_blank(newdata[[col]])) {
      to_expand <- c(to_expand, col)
    }
  }

  if (length(to_expand)) {
    levels_list <- lapply(to_expand, function(col) fit_levels(fit, col))
    names(levels_list) <- to_expand
    keep <- vapply(levels_list, length, integer(1L)) > 0L
    levels_list <- levels_list[keep]
    to_expand <- names(levels_list)
  }

  if (length(to_expand)) {
    grid <- do.call(tidyr::expand_grid, levels_list)
    rest <- newdata[, setdiff(names(newdata), to_expand), drop = FALSE]
    out <- dplyr::bind_cols(
      rest[rep(1L, nrow(grid)), , drop = FALSE],
      grid
    )
  } else {
    out <- newdata
  }

  if (is.null(new_level_tag)) {
    new_level_tag <- sprintf(
      "__new__%d_%d",
      as.integer(Sys.time()),
      sample.int(1e6, 1L)
    )
  }
  for (col in new_level_cols) {
    if (col %in% fit_vars) out[[col]] <- new_level_tag
  }

  tibble::as_tibble(out)
}

# Posterior predictive comparison of obs against a brms fit.
#   - posterior_predict (NOT epred): include likelihood noise so tail tests
#     are calibrated against new-observation predictive intervals.
#   - re_formula = NULL: keep tissue_groups random slopes (observed level).
#   - allow_new_levels + sample_new_levels = "uncertainty": dataset_id_altered
#     gets a new draw from its random-intercept population per posterior draw.
#   - marginalize_over: unknown covariates are integrated out by uniform
#     mixture over training-set levels.
gene_deviation_from_fit <- function(
  fit,
  newdata,
  obs,
  cred_mass = 0.95,
  alpha = 0.025,
  marginalize_over = c("sex", "age_decade", "ethnicity_groups", "assay_groups_altered"),
  required = c("tissue_groups", "offset", "disease_groups_altered"),
  new_level_cols = "dataset_id_altered",
  new_level_tag = NULL,
  re_formula = NULL,
  allow_new_levels = TRUE,
  sample_new_levels = "uncertainty"
) {
  nd_grid <- build_newdata_grid(
    fit,
    newdata,
    marginalize_over = marginalize_over,
    required = required,
    new_level_cols = new_level_cols,
    new_level_tag = new_level_tag
  )

  y_rep_mat <- brms::posterior_predict(
    fit,
    newdata = nd_grid,
    summary = FALSE,
    re_formula = re_formula,
    allow_new_levels = allow_new_levels,
    sample_new_levels = sample_new_levels
  )

  y_rep <- as.numeric(y_rep_mat)

  hpd <- if (requireNamespace("HDInterval", quietly = TRUE)) {
    HDInterval::hdi(y_rep, credMass = cred_mass)
  } else {
    probs <- c((1 - cred_mass) / 2, 1 - (1 - cred_mass) / 2)
    stats::quantile(y_rep, probs = probs, names = FALSE)
  }

  p_above <- mean(y_rep >= obs)
  p_below <- mean(y_rep <= obs)

  tibble::tibble(
    observed_count = obs,
    healthy_median = median(y_rep),
    healthy_mean = mean(y_rep),
    healthy_hpd_lo = hpd[1],
    healthy_hpd_hi = hpd[2],
    obs_percentile = mean(y_rep <= obs),
    p_above_healthy = p_above,
    p_below_healthy = p_below,
    posterior_tail_p = 2 * min(p_above, p_below),
    log2fc_vs_median = log2((obs + 1) / (median(y_rep) + 1)),
    n_grid_rows = NROW(nd_grid),
    direction = dplyr::case_when(
      p_above < alpha ~ "higher_than_healthy",
      p_below < alpha ~ "lower_than_healthy",
      TRUE ~ "consistent_with_healthy"
    )
  )
}
```

```{r}
#| label: predict-sting-vs-healthy
#| cache: false

handlers("progress")

sting_fit_rows <- sting_estimates_chunk |>
  dplyr::filter(.data$compression_ok == TRUE) |>
  dplyr::filter(lengths(.data$brms_fit_compressed) > 0L) |>
  dplyr::filter(.data$.feature %in% rownames(se_monocytic))

if (!nrow(sting_fit_rows)) {
  stop("No compressed biomarker fits available; run with params$run_fits: true or fix estimates_rds.")
}

with_progress({
  p <- progressr::progressor(steps = nrow(sting_fit_rows) * nrow(comparison_samples_tbl))

  gene_deviation_all <- purrr::imap_dfr(
    seq_len(nrow(sting_fit_rows)),
    function(i, idx) {
      chunk_row <- sting_fit_rows[i, ]
      feature_id <- chunk_row$.feature
      gene_sym <- chunk_row$gene
      fit <- poco::reconstruct_brmsfit(chunk_row$brms_fit_compressed[[1]])

      purrr::pmap_dfr(
        comparison_samples_tbl |>
          dplyr::select("sample", "sample_idx", "sample_role"),
        function(sample, sample_idx, sample_role) {
          p()

          newdata <- newdata_for_sample(se_monocytic, sample_idx)
          obs <-
            SummarizedExperiment::assay(
              se_monocytic[feature_id, sample_idx, drop = FALSE],
              "counts"
            ) |>
            as.numeric()

          gene_deviation_from_fit(
            fit,
            newdata,
            obs,
            new_level_tag = paste0("__savi__", as.character(sample))
            # sample_new_levels = 'gaussian'
          ) |>
            dplyr::mutate(
              .feature = feature_id,
              gene = gene_sym,
              sample = as.character(sample),
              sample_role = as.character(sample_role),
              .before = "observed_count"
            )
        }
      )
    }
  )
})

gene_deviation_all <- gene_deviation_all |>
  tibble::as_tibble() |>
  dplyr::select(tidyselect::where(\(x) !is.list(x)))

if (!"sample_role" %in% colnames(gene_deviation_all)) {
  gene_deviation_all <- gene_deviation_all |>
    dplyr::left_join(
      comparison_samples_tbl |>
        dplyr::select("sample", "sample_role"),
      by = "sample"
    )
}

gene_deviation_all
```

# Evaluate deviations against the published STING signature

De Cevins *et al.* (2023) define a **21-gene STING-activation module** that is **up in disease-associated monocytes from SAVI patients relative to healthy controls** in the same cohort (Figure 6; Table S6)—after removing IFN-β–inducible genes. Our posterior test asks a **different** question: whether each pseudobulk count lies above the **Immune Atlas healthy predictive** distribution for monocytic cells, given donor metadata. We still expect:

| `Category` (study cohort) | Paper-consistent expectation for signature genes |
|---------------------------|---------------------------------------------------|
| **`SAVI`** | Mostly **`higher_than_healthy`** vs atlas baseline |
| **`CTRL`** | Mostly **`consistent_with_healthy`** (study controls without STING activation) |
| **`SAVI_treated`** | Intermediate—treatment samples often move toward baseline (we score **`consistent_with_healthy`** as the nominal match, same as controls) |

Sample **`Category`** comes from the GEO Seurat object (`prepare_data.R`) and is carried in **`colData(se_monocytic)`** (`CTRL`, `SAVI`, `SAVI_treated`; reference columns are **`NA`**).

```{r}
#| label: sting-literature-eval
sample_annotations <- cd_mono |>
  dplyr::filter(.data$sample_role == "savi_pseudobulk") |>
  dplyr::select(
    "sample",
    "Sample",
    "Category",
    tidyselect::any_of("Treatment")
  ) |>
  dplyr::distinct() |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    Category = factor(
      .data$Category,
      levels = c("CTRL", "SAVI", "SAVI_treated")
    )
  )

category_expected <- tibble::tribble(
  ~Category,        ~expected_deviation,
  "CTRL",           "consistent_with_healthy",
  "SAVI",           "higher_than_healthy",
  "SAVI_treated",   "consistent_with_healthy"
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(Category = factor(.data$Category, levels = levels(sample_annotations$Category)))

gene_deviation_eval <- gene_deviation_savi |>
  dplyr::left_join(sample_annotations, by = "sample") |>
  dplyr::left_join(category_expected, by = "Category") |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    deviation_score = dplyr::case_when(
      .data$direction == "higher_than_healthy" ~ 1L,
      .data$direction == "lower_than_healthy" ~ -1L,
      TRUE ~ 0L
    ),
    matches_literature = dplyr::case_when(
      is.na(.data$expected_deviation) ~ NA,
      .data$expected_deviation == .data$direction ~ TRUE,
      TRUE ~ FALSE
    ),
    signature_up = .data$direction == "higher_than_healthy"
  )

signature_by_sample <- gene_deviation_eval |>
  dplyr::group_by(.data$sample, .data$Sample, .data$Category) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    n_genes = dplyr::n(),
    n_higher = sum(.data$signature_up),
    n_lower = sum(.data$direction == "lower_than_healthy"),
    n_consistent = sum(.data$direction == "consistent_with_healthy"),
    pct_higher = 100 * .data$n_higher / .data$n_genes,
    pct_match = 100 * mean(.data$matches_literature, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_log2fc = mean(.data$log2fc_vs_median, na.rm = TRUE),
    signature_score = mean(.data$deviation_score, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

agreement_by_category <- gene_deviation_eval |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(.data$Category), !is.na(.data$expected_deviation)) |>
  dplyr::group_by(.data$Category, .data$expected_deviation) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    n_tests = dplyr::n(),
    n_match = sum(.data$matches_literature, na.rm = TRUE),
    pct_match = 100 * .data$n_match / .data$n_tests,
    pct_higher = 100 * mean(.data$signature_up),
    pct_consistent = 100 * mean(.data$direction == "consistent_with_healthy"),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

agreement_by_category
```

# Biomarker quality check (atlas-based falsification)

De Cevins *et al.* (2023) propose the **21-gene signature** by **within-cohort comparison** (5 SAVI vs 7 in-study controls). With only seven matched donors, a gene that is simply **variable in healthy people** but happened to be low in their controls can pass that filter. We can sanity-check each signature gene against a much broader **healthy reference** (Immune Atlas monocytic posteriors), which is the kind of falsification their paper could not do. The expected pattern under a true SAVI biomarker is:

- **SAVI** samples → consistently **higher** than the atlas healthy distribution
- **SAVI_treated** samples → **intermediate** (attenuated by treatment)
- **CTRL** samples → **consistent with healthy** (atlas baseline matches the in-cohort controls)

A gene fails the check (paper-supported but **not** atlas-supported) when:

- **CTRL drifts up** vs atlas (gene is high in many healthy people, not just SAVI),
- **No SAVI lift** vs CTRL (paper effect is within healthy variability),
- **SAVI_treated ≥ SAVI** (no treatment effect even though paper claims one).

```{r}
#| label: biomarker-per-category
biomarker_per_category <- gene_deviation_eval |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(.data$Category)) |>
  dplyr::group_by(.data$gene, .data$Category) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    n_samples = dplyr::n_distinct(.data$sample),
    mean_log2fc = mean(.data$log2fc_vs_median, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_log2fc = stats::median(.data$log2fc_vs_median, na.rm = TRUE),
    pct_higher = 100 * mean(.data$direction == "higher_than_healthy"),
    pct_lower = 100 * mean(.data$direction == "lower_than_healthy"),
    pct_consistent = 100 * mean(.data$direction == "consistent_with_healthy"),
    mean_p_above_healthy = mean(.data$p_above_healthy, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

biomarker_per_category |>
  dplyr::arrange(.data$gene, .data$Category)
```

```{r}
#| label: biomarker-quality-score
biomarker_quality <- biomarker_per_category |>
  dplyr::select(
    "gene",
    "Category",
    "mean_log2fc",
    "pct_higher",
    "pct_consistent"
  ) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(
    names_from = "Category",
    values_from = c("mean_log2fc", "pct_higher", "pct_consistent"),
    values_fill = NA_real_,
    names_sep = "."
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    savi_lift = .data$mean_log2fc.SAVI,
    ctrl_drift = .data$mean_log2fc.CTRL,
    treated_lift = .data$mean_log2fc.SAVI_treated,

    # SAVI vs in-cohort controls' atlas-corrected position (paper's main claim).
    savi_vs_ctrl = .data$savi_lift - .data$ctrl_drift,

    # Treatment effect: positive means SAVI_treated drops back toward baseline.
    treatment_attenuation = .data$savi_lift - .data$treated_lift,

    # Atlas baseline agreement of in-study controls (closer to 0 = better).
    abs_ctrl_drift = abs(.data$ctrl_drift),

    # Composite quality: reward SAVI > CTRL, reward treatment drop,
    # penalise CTRL drift from atlas. Weights chosen so all three terms are on
    # the log2 scale; tweak if needed.
    quality_score = .data$savi_vs_ctrl +
      0.5 * .data$treatment_attenuation -
      0.5 * .data$abs_ctrl_drift,

    biomarker_class = dplyr::case_when(
      .data$pct_higher.SAVI >= 60 &
        .data$pct_consistent.CTRL >= 50 &
        .data$treatment_attenuation > 0 ~ "validated",
      .data$pct_higher.SAVI >= 60 &
        .data$treatment_attenuation > 0 &
        .data$pct_consistent.CTRL < 50 ~ "validated_ctrl_drifts",
      .data$pct_higher.SAVI >= 60 &
        .data$treatment_attenuation <= 0 ~ "savi_up_no_treatment_effect",
      .data$pct_higher.SAVI < 30 &
        .data$ctrl_drift > 0.5 ~ "falsified_baseline_high",
      .data$pct_higher.SAVI < 30 ~ "falsified_no_savi_signal",
      TRUE ~ "ambiguous"
    )
  ) |>
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(.data$quality_score))

biomarker_quality |>
  dplyr::select(
    "gene",
    "biomarker_class",
    "quality_score",
    "savi_vs_ctrl",
    "treatment_attenuation",
    "abs_ctrl_drift",
    dplyr::starts_with("pct_higher."),
    dplyr::starts_with("pct_consistent.")
  )
```

```{r}
class_levels <- c(
  "validated",
  "validated_ctrl_drifts",

class_cols <- c(
  validated = "#1a9850",
  validated_ctrl_drifts = "#66bd63",
  savi_up_no_treatment_effect = "#fee08b",
  ambiguous = "#bdbdbd",
  falsified_baseline_high = "#762a83",
  falsified_no_savi_signal = "#d73027"
)

ggplot2::ggplot(
  biomarker_quality |>
    dplyr::mutate(

    y = NULL,
```

```{r}
#| label: biomarker-falsified-genes
biomarker_quality |>
  dplyr::filter(.data$biomarker_class %in% c(
    "falsified_no_savi_signal",
    "falsified_baseline_high",
    "savi_up_no_treatment_effect"
  )) |>
  dplyr::select(
    "gene",
    "biomarker_class",
    "savi_lift",
    "ctrl_drift",
    "treated_lift",
    "pct_higher.SAVI",
    "pct_higher.CTRL",
    "pct_consistent.CTRL"
  ) |>
  dplyr::arrange(.data$biomarker_class, .data$gene)
```

**Interpretation:**

- **`validated`** — gene behaves as the paper claims and is **also** consistent with the atlas (high in SAVI, attenuated by treatment, in-cohort controls match atlas baseline). Strong biomarker.
- **`validated_ctrl_drifts`** — gene goes up in SAVI and drops with treatment, but the paper's controls are already above the atlas baseline. The within-cohort effect is real; absolute reference value should be interpreted with care.
- **`savi_up_no_treatment_effect`** — SAVI lift exists but treatment doesn't move it. The gene may be a state marker rather than an activity readout.
- **`ambiguous`** — borderline; needs more samples.
- **`falsified_baseline_high`** — gene reads as high in study controls *and* in the broader atlas, and SAVI doesn't add much on top. The paper's "up in SAVI" is likely a baseline artefact.
- **`falsified_no_savi_signal`** — no SAVI lift vs atlas at all. Strong falsification candidate.

This is the kind of cross-study check the original paper could not perform because of the small healthy-cohort size.

# Case study: falsifying *IL1B*

**IL1B** is the clearest atlas-falsified gene in this cohort: study **controls sit above** the Immune Atlas healthy predictive distribution, while **SAVI samples do not sit higher still**. That pattern breaks the signature logic (“up in patients vs healthy”) when “healthy” is the atlas rather than seven matched donors.

To make the falsification auditable we show:

1. **Per-sample posterior predictive checks** — observed count vs healthy HPD (already computed).
2. **Predictive densities** — draw-level `posterior_predict` for IL1B vs a **validated** contrast gene (**TSC22D2**).
3. **Three reference frames** — atlas-corrected mean log2 FC vs **within-cohort** category means (raw and TMM-scaled counts averaged over donors in each `Category` only; no atlas comparison on the paper panels).

```{r}
#| label: il1b-falsify-helpers
falsify_contrast_genes <- c("IL1B", "TSC22D2")

scaled_counts_assay_name <- function(se) {
  nms <- SummarizedExperiment::assayNames(se)
  if ("counts_scaled" %in% nms) {
    return("counts_scaled")
  }
  stop(
    "Assay `counts_scaled` not found on `se_monocytic`. ",
    "Run the `scale-abundance` chunk first."
  )
}

il1b_ensembl <- sting_signature_21 |>
  dplyr::filter(.data$gene == "IL1B") |>
  dplyr::pull(.feature)

il1b_scaled_obs <- tibble::tibble(sample = colnames(se_monocytic)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    sample_idx = match(.data$sample, colnames(se_monocytic)),
    observed_scaled = as.numeric(
      SummarizedExperiment::assay(
        se_monocytic[il1b_ensembl, .data$sample_idx, drop = FALSE],
        scaled_counts_assay_name(se_monocytic)
      )
    )
  )

il1b_sample_tbl <- gene_deviation_eval |>
  dplyr::filter(.data$gene == "IL1B", !is.na(.data$Category)) |>
  dplyr::left_join(
    sample_annotations |>
      dplyr::select("sample", tidyselect::any_of("Treatment")),
    by = "sample"
  ) |>
  dplyr::left_join(il1b_scaled_obs, by = "sample") |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    Category = factor(.data$Category, levels = names(category_cols)),
    # Map count-scale predictive summaries to TMM-scaled scale (per-sample ratio).
    scale_ratio = .data$observed_scaled / pmax(.data$observed_count, 1e-9),
    healthy_median_scaled = .data$healthy_median * .data$scale_ratio,
    healthy_hpd_lo_scaled = .data$healthy_hpd_lo * .data$scale_ratio,
    healthy_hpd_hi_scaled = .data$healthy_hpd_hi * .data$scale_ratio,
    above_hpd = .data$observed_scaled > .data$healthy_hpd_hi_scaled,
    below_hpd = .data$observed_scaled < .data$healthy_hpd_lo_scaled,
    in_hpd = !.data$above_hpd & !.data$below_hpd
  ) |>
  dplyr::arrange(.data$Category, .data$Sample)

il1b_sample_tbl |>
  dplyr::select(
    "Sample",
    "Category",
    "observed_scaled",
    "healthy_median_scaled",
    "healthy_hpd_lo_scaled",
    "healthy_hpd_hi_scaled",
    "obs_percentile",
    "direction",
    "log2fc_vs_median"
  )
```

```{r}
  ) +
```

```{r}
        dplyr::pull(Sample) |>
        unique()
    )
  ) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(
    cols = c("observed_count", "observed_scaled"),
    names_to = "measure",
    values_to = "abundance"
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    measure = dplyr::recode(
      .data$measure,
      observed_count = "Raw pseudobulk counts",
      observed_scaled = "TMM-scaled counts"
    ),
    measure = factor(
      .data$measure,
      levels = c("Raw pseudobulk counts", "TMM-scaled counts")
    )
  )

log1p_trans <- scales::trans_new(
  name = "log1p",
  transform = function(x) log1p(pmax(x, 0)),
  inverse = function(x) expm1(x),
  domain = c(0, Inf)
)

ggplot2::ggplot(
  il1b_counts_long,
  ggplot2::aes(
    x = sample_label,
    y = abundance,
    colour = Category
  )
) +
  ggplot2::geom_point(size = 3.5) +
  ggplot2::facet_wrap(~measure, scales = "free_y", ncol = 2) +
  ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(trans = log1p_trans) +
  ggplot2::scale_colour_manual(values = category_cols) +
  ggplot2::labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = expression(log[1 + p]("count")),
    title = expression(italic("IL1B") * ": per-donor abundance (raw vs TMM-scaled)"),
    subtitle = paste0(
      "Each point = one donor pseudobulk in the GSE226598 cohort (not a category mean). ",
      "Atlas percentile is identical on both scales (linear TMM rescaling); ",
      "see obs_percentile in the table above."
    )
  ) +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  ggplot2::theme(
    axis.text.x = ggplot2::element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 8),
    legend.position = "top",
    strip.text = ggplot2::element_text(size = 10)
  )
```

```{r}
#| label: il1b-predictive-draws
#| cache: true

# Subsampled posterior_predict draws for density overlays (IL1B vs TSC22D2).
# Model scale = raw pseudobulk counts (same as atlas posterior_predict).
predictive_draws_raw_for_gene <- function(
  gene_sym,
  se,
  comparison_tbl,
  sample_ann,
  ndraws = 400L
) {
  chunk_row <- sting_fit_rows |>
    dplyr::filter(.data$gene == .env$gene_sym) |>
    dplyr::slice(1)

  if (!nrow(chunk_row)) {
    stop("No fit found for gene: ", gene_sym)
  }

  fit <- poco::reconstruct_brmsfit(chunk_row$brms_fit_compressed[[1]])
  feature_id <- chunk_row$.feature

  purrr::pmap_dfr(
    comparison_tbl |>
      dplyr::filter(.data$sample_role == "savi_pseudobulk") |>
      dplyr::select("sample", "sample_idx"),
    function(sample, sample_idx) {
      newdata <- newdata_for_sample(se, sample_idx)
      nd_grid <- build_newdata_grid(
        fit,
        newdata,
        new_level_tag = paste0("__savi__", as.character(sample))
      )

      y_rep <- brms::posterior_predict(
        fit,
        newdata = nd_grid,
        summary = FALSE,
        re_formula = NULL,
        allow_new_levels = TRUE,
        sample_new_levels = "uncertainty",
        ndraws = ndraws
      ) |>
        as.numeric()

      obs_raw <- SummarizedExperiment::assay(
        se[feature_id, sample_idx, drop = FALSE],
        "counts"
      ) |>
        as.numeric()

      tibble::tibble(
        gene = gene_sym,
        sample = as.character(sample),
        draw = y_rep,
        observed_count = obs_raw
      )
    }
  ) |>
    dplyr::left_join(
      sample_ann |>
        dplyr::select("sample", "Sample", "Category"),
      by = "sample"
    )
}

contrast_draws <- purrr::map_dfr(
  falsify_contrast_genes,
  predictive_draws_raw_for_gene,
  se = se_monocytic,
  comparison_tbl = comparison_samples_tbl,
  sample_ann = sample_annotations
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    Category = factor(.data$Category, levels = names(category_cols)),
    gene = factor(.data$gene, levels = falsify_contrast_genes),
    draw_log1p = log1p(pmax(.data$draw, 0)),
    observed_log1p = log1p(pmax(.data$observed_count, 0))
  )

contrast_draws |>
  dplyr::count(.data$gene, .data$Category, name = "n_draws")
```

```{r}
il1b_ctrl_vs_savi <- il1b_sample_tbl |>
  dplyr::group_by(.data$Category) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    n = dplyr::n(),
    mean_obs = mean(.data$observed_count),

    pct_above_hpd = 100 * mean(.data$above_hpd),
    pct_higher_direction = 100 * mean(.data$direction == "higher_than_healthy"),
    mean_percentile = 100 * mean(.data$obs_percentile),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

ctrl_mean_log2fc <- il1b_ctrl_vs_savi |>
  dplyr::filter(.data$Category == "CTRL") |>
  dplyr::pull(.data$mean_log2fc)

ctrl_pct_above_hpd <- il1b_ctrl_vs_savi |>
  dplyr::filter(.data$Category == "CTRL") |>
  dplyr::pull(.data$pct_above_hpd)

savi_pct_above_hpd <- il1b_ctrl_vs_savi |>
  dplyr::filter(.data$Category == "SAVI") |>
  dplyr::pull(.data$pct_above_hpd)

paper_delta <- il1b_ctrl_vs_savi |>
  dplyr::filter(.data$Category %in% c("SAVI", "CTRL")) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = "Category", values_from = "mean_obs") |>
  dplyr::mutate(delta = .data$SAVI - .data$CTRL) |>
  dplyr::pull(.data$delta)

atlas_delta <- biomarker_quality |>
  dplyr::filter(.data$gene == "IL1B") |>
  dplyr::pull(.data$savi_vs_ctrl)

tibble::tibble(
  gene = "IL1B",
  paper_mean_savi_minus_ctrl_raw_counts = paper_delta,
  atlas_mean_log2fc_savi_minus_ctrl = atlas_delta,
  ctrl_pct_above_healthy_hpd = ctrl_pct_above_hpd,
  savi_pct_above_healthy_hpd = savi_pct_above_hpd,
  falsification_verdict = dplyr::if_else(
    is.finite(atlas_delta) &&
      atlas_delta < 0 &&
      is.finite(ctrl_mean_log2fc) &&
      ctrl_mean_log2fc > 0,
    "Atlas falsified: controls high, SAVI not elevated after correction",
    "Review manually"
  )
)

il1b_ctrl_vs_savi
```

**How to read this as falsification evidence**

- **Per-donor plots** (HPD, raw/scaled abundance, density facets): each point/line is one pseudobulk library; HPD and density overlays use **raw counts** on the model scale (`posterior_predict` draws and observed `counts` assay). The two-panel abundance plot shows the same donors on **raw** and **TMM-scaled** count scales (log1p y-axis); atlas percentile is unchanged under linear scaling.
- **Bar chart (`plot-il1b-two-nulls`)**: height = **mean within the GSE226598 cohort** for donors in that `Category` only (not vs atlas on the two right panels). Left panel = mean log2(obs / atlas predictive median); centre = mean raw pseudobulk count; right = mean log1p(TMM-scaled count).
- If **atlas falsification holds**: per-donor plots show **CTRL** above the atlas HPD and high `obs_percentile` in the table above, while **SAVI** is not systematically above CTRL on the **left bar panel** (mean log2 FC).
- The **centre bar panel** can still show **SAVI > CTRL** on raw within-cohort means — the contrast the original paper could see with seven controls.
- The **summary table** quantifies: `paper_mean_savi_minus_ctrl_raw_counts` can stay **positive** while `atlas_mean_log2fc_savi_minus_ctrl` is **negative**.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Case study: falsifying *ADRB2* (one-donor SAVI signal)

**ADRB2** is labelled **`falsified_no_savi_signal`** in the biomarker screen because only **20%** of SAVI donors pass the strict atlas tail call (`higher_than_healthy`), yet the **cohort mean** `log2fc_vs_median` in SAVI looks high. That pattern usually means **one outlier donor** pulls the category mean while the other SAVI pseudobulks sit near the healthy predictive null.

We audit that claim with per-donor tables, leave-one-out SAVI means, and density overlays on **raw pseudobulk counts** (same scale as `posterior_predict`; contrast gene **TSC22D2** = validated atlas behaviour).

```{r}
#| label: adrb2-falsify-helpers

adrb2_ensembl <- sting_signature_21 |>
  dplyr::filter(.data$gene == "ADRB2") |>
  dplyr::pull(.feature)

adrb2_scaled_obs <- tibble::tibble(sample = colnames(se_monocytic)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    sample_idx = match(.data$sample, colnames(se_monocytic)),
    observed_scaled = as.numeric(
      SummarizedExperiment::assay(
        se_monocytic[adrb2_ensembl, .data$sample_idx, drop = FALSE],
        scaled_counts_assay_name(se_monocytic)
      )
    )
  )

adrb2_sample_tbl <- gene_deviation_eval |>
  dplyr::filter(.data$gene == "ADRB2", !is.na(.data$Category)) |>
  dplyr::left_join(
    sample_annotations |>
      dplyr::select("sample", tidyselect::any_of("Treatment")),
    by = "sample"
  ) |>
  dplyr::left_join(adrb2_scaled_obs, by = "sample") |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    Category = factor(.data$Category, levels = names(category_cols)),
    scale_ratio = .data$observed_scaled / pmax(.data$observed_count, 1e-9),
    healthy_median_scaled = .data$healthy_median * .data$scale_ratio,
    healthy_hpd_lo_scaled = .data$healthy_hpd_lo * .data$scale_ratio,
    healthy_hpd_hi_scaled = .data$healthy_hpd_hi * .data$scale_ratio,
    above_hpd = .data$observed_count > .data$healthy_hpd_hi,
    below_hpd = .data$observed_count < .data$healthy_hpd_lo,
    in_hpd = !.data$above_hpd & !.data$below_hpd
  ) |>
  dplyr::arrange(.data$Category, .data$Sample)

adrb2_savi_tbl <- adrb2_sample_tbl |>
  dplyr::filter(.data$Category == "SAVI")

adrb2_savi_outlier_pick <- adrb2_savi_tbl |>
  dplyr::filter(.data$direction == "higher_than_healthy") |>
  dplyr::slice(1)

if (nrow(adrb2_savi_outlier_pick) == 0L) {
  adrb2_savi_outlier_pick <- adrb2_savi_tbl |>
    dplyr::slice_max(.data$log2fc_vs_median, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE)
}

adrb2_label_levels <- adrb2_sample_tbl |>
  dplyr::arrange(.data$Category, .data$Sample)

adrb2_sample_tbl <- adrb2_sample_tbl |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    savi_outlier = .data$sample %in% adrb2_savi_outlier_pick$sample,
    direction_short = dplyr::case_when(
      .data$direction == "higher_than_healthy" ~ "higher",
      .data$direction == "lower_than_healthy" ~ "lower",
      TRUE ~ "consistent"
    ),
    sample_facet_label = paste0(
      .data$Sample,
      " (",
      .data$Category,
      " · ",
      .data$direction_short,
      ", p=",
      sprintf("%.2f", .data$p_above_healthy),
      ")"
    ),
    sample_label = factor(
      .data$sample_facet_label,
      levels = adrb2_label_levels |>
        dplyr::mutate(
          lab = paste0(
            .data$Sample,
            " (",
            .data$Category,
            " · ",
            dplyr::case_when(
              .data$direction == "higher_than_healthy" ~ "higher",
              .data$direction == "lower_than_healthy" ~ "lower",
              TRUE ~ "consistent"
            ),
            ", p=",
            sprintf("%.2f", .data$p_above_healthy),
            ")"
          )
        ) |>
        dplyr::pull(.data$lab)
    )
  )

adrb2_savi_outlier <- adrb2_sample_tbl |>
  dplyr::filter(.data$savi_outlier)

adrb2_loo_summary <- tibble::tibble(
  contrast = c(
    "All SAVI donors",
    "Drop atlas-tail SAVI donor",
    "Other SAVI donors (median)"
  ),
  n_savi = c(
    nrow(adrb2_savi_tbl),
    nrow(adrb2_savi_tbl) - 1L,
    nrow(adrb2_savi_tbl) - 1L
  ),
  mean_log2fc = c(
    mean(adrb2_savi_tbl$log2fc_vs_median),
    mean(
      adrb2_savi_tbl$log2fc_vs_median[
        adrb2_savi_tbl$sample != adrb2_savi_outlier$sample
      ]
    ),
    stats::median(
      adrb2_savi_tbl$log2fc_vs_median[
        adrb2_savi_tbl$sample != adrb2_savi_outlier$sample
      ]
    )
  ),
  pct_higher = c(
    100 * mean(adrb2_savi_tbl$direction == "higher_than_healthy"),
    100 * mean(
      adrb2_savi_tbl$direction[
        adrb2_savi_tbl$sample != adrb2_savi_outlier$sample
      ] == "higher_than_healthy"
    ),
    NA_real_
  )
)

adrb2_per_donor <- adrb2_sample_tbl |>
  dplyr::select(
    Sample,
    Category,
    direction,
    direction_short,
    p_above_healthy,
    log2fc_vs_median,
    obs_percentile,
    observed_count,
    observed_scaled,
    savi_outlier,
    sample_facet_label
  )

adrb2_per_donor

adrb2_loo_summary

tibble::tibble(
  outlier_sample = adrb2_savi_outlier$Sample,
  outlier_direction = adrb2_savi_outlier$direction,
  outlier_log2fc = adrb2_savi_outlier$log2fc_vs_median,

  n_savi_consistent = sum(adrb2_savi_tbl$direction == "consistent_with_healthy"),
  biomarker_class = biomarker_quality |>

    dplyr::pull(.data$biomarker_class)
)
```

```{r}
  ggplot2::geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = 2, colour = "grey45") +
  ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(values = c("#E41A1C", "#FC8D59", "#FDBB84"), guide = "none") +
  ggplot2::labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = expression("Mean / median " * log[2] * " FC (SAVI only)"),
    title = expression(italic("ADRB2") * ": SAVI cohort mean driven by one donor"),
    subtitle = paste0(
      "Dropping ",
      adrb2_savi_outlier$Sample,
      " collapses the SAVI mean toward 0; remaining donors do not support a cohort-wide atlas tail."
    )
  ) +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  ggplot2::theme(axis.text.x = ggplot2::element_text(angle = 25, hjust = 1))
```

**How to read**

- **`plot-adrb2-log2fc-by-sample`** and **`plot-adrb2-density-facet-sample`**: same **raw-count** scale as the atlas model; facet labels show **atlas tail** and **`p = P(draw >= obs)`**. Only **P6_STING_ht** has **p < 0.025** (thicker line).
- **`plot-adrb2-leave-one-out`**: removing that donor drops the SAVI mean `log2fc` toward zero (median of the remaining four is lower still).
- **Density panels**: pooled SAVI curve for *ADRB2* can look elevated because draws are stacked across donors; per-donor facets show the mismatch between one extreme line and four lines near the grey null.
- **Single-cell UMAP** (below, with *IL1B*): SCT-normalized *ADRB2* on disease-associated monocytes, split by **`Category`**, to see whether the atlas outlier is visible at cell level or confined to one donor's monocytes.

# Single-cell expression on UMAP (GEO Seurat object)

Published scRNA-seq object [GSE226598](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE226598) (`prepare_data.R`). We subset **`params$savi_sc_celltype`** (disease-associated monocytes — same population as the pseudobulk merge) and plot signature genes on the embedded UMAP, **`split.by = "Category"`** (`CTRL`, `SAVI`, `SAVI_treated`), using the **`SCT`** assay **`data`** slot (SCTransform–normalized expression from the published object).

```{r}
#| label: load-savi-seurat
#| cache: false

read_geo_rds_gz <- function(path) {
  con <- gzcon(gzfile(path))
  on.exit(close(con), add = TRUE)
  readRDS(con)
}

seurat_savi <- read_geo_rds_gz(params$savi_seurat_gz)

if (!"Category" %in% colnames(seurat_savi@meta.data)) {
  stop("`Category` not found in Seurat metadata.")
}

seurat_savi$Category <- factor(
  seurat_savi$Category,
  levels = c("CTRL", "SAVI", "SAVI_treated")
)

seurat_reduction <- function(se) {
  nms <- names(se@reductions)
  hit <- intersect(c("umap", "UMAP", "tsne", "TSNE"), nms)
  if (length(hit)) {
    return(hit[[1]])
  }
  nms[[1]]
}

reduction_use <- seurat_reduction(seurat_savi)

# Subset early so we don't keep the full >2k x 24k object around.
seurat_savi_mono <- seurat_savi |>
  subset(CellType == params$savi_sc_celltype)
# rm(seurat_savi)
# gc(verbose = FALSE)

tibble::tibble(
  n_cells = ncol(seurat_savi_mono),
  reduction = reduction_use,
  categories = paste(levels(seurat_savi_mono$Category), collapse = ", "),
  il1b_present = "IL1B" %in% rownames(seurat_savi_mono),
  adrb2_present = "ADRB2" %in% rownames(seurat_savi_mono)
)
```

```{r}

  stop(
    "No cells for CellType = '", params$savi_sc_celltype,
    "'. Check `CellType` levels in the Seurat object."
  )
}

seurat_savi_mono$Category <- factor(
  seurat_savi_mono$Category,
  levels = c("CTRL", "SAVI", "SAVI_treated")
)

tibble::tibble(
  cell_type = params$savi_sc_celltype,
  n_cells = ncol(seurat_savi_mono)
)

table(seurat_savi_mono$Category, useNA = "ifany")
```

```{r}
Seurat::FeaturePlot(
```

Panel titles are **`Category`** (study cohort label from GEO metadata). Expression is from **SCTransform** (`assay = "SCT"`, `slot = "data"`), not raw **`RNA`** counts. High **`IL1B`** in **CTRL** monocytes complements the pseudobulk / atlas falsification checks above.

#### *ADRB2* on UMAP (all donors)

Same layout as *IL1B*: disease-associated monocytes, SCT **`data`**, **`split.by = "Category"`**. Compare the **SAVI** column to **CTRL** and **SAVI_treated** — cells from all donors in each arm are pooled on the UMAP.

```{r}
#| label: plot-adrb2-featureplot-category
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 4
#| fig-align: center

if (!"ADRB2" %in% rownames(seurat_savi_mono[["SCT"]])) {
  stop("ADRB2 not found in SCT assay rownames.")
}

Seurat::FeaturePlot(
  seurat_savi_mono,
  features = "ADRB2",
  assay = "SCT",
  split.by = "Category",
  reduction = reduction_use,
  slot = "data",
  ncol = 3,
  order = TRUE,
  pt.size = 0.35,
  min.cutoff = "q10",
  max.cutoff = "q90"
) &
  ggplot2::theme(
    plot.title = ggplot2::element_text(size = 11),
    strip.text = ggplot2::element_text(size = 11, face = "bold")
  )
```

The **SAVI** panel above pools monocytes from all five untreated SAVI donors. Pseudobulk checks show atlas deviation is dominated by **`P6_STING_ht`** (4057 raw counts, **`p_above_healthy < 0.025`**); the other four SAVI donors sit near the healthy null (≤65 raw counts). If **`ADRB2`** signal in **SAVI** is sparse overall but driven by cells from that donor, the pooled UMAP can still look elevated.

#### *ADRB2* after removing the atlas-tail donor

Mirroring **`plot-adrb2-leave-one-out`** on pseudobulk, we repeat the UMAP with **every disease-associated monocyte from the atlas-tail SAVI donor removed** (`adrb2_savi_outlier$Sample`, here **`P6_STING_ht`**). Assay, cell type, and **`split.by = "Category"`** are unchanged; only that library’s cells are dropped, so the **SAVI** facet reflects the remaining four untreated SAVI donors. If the **SAVI** panel now resembles **CTRL** / **SAVI_treated**, the cohort-level **`ADRB2`** signal is a **one-donor** artefact at single-cell resolution as well as in pseudobulk.

```{r}
#| label: plot-adrb2-featureplot-category_outlier_removed
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 4
#| fig-align: center

if (!"ADRB2" %in% rownames(seurat_savi_mono[["SCT"]])) {
  stop("ADRB2 not found in SCT assay rownames.")
}

if (!"Sample" %in% colnames(seurat_savi_mono@meta.data)) {
  stop("`Sample` not found in Seurat metadata.")
}

outlier_sample <- adrb2_savi_outlier$Sample

seurat_savi_mono_no_outlier <- subset(
  seurat_savi_mono,
  subset = Sample != outlier_sample
)

Seurat::FeaturePlot(
  seurat_savi_mono_no_outlier,
  features = "ADRB2",
  assay = "SCT",
  split.by = "Category",
  reduction = reduction_use,
  slot = "data",
  ncol = 3,
  order = TRUE,
  pt.size = 0.35,
  min.cutoff = "q10",
  max.cutoff = "q90"
) &
  ggplot2::theme(
    plot.title = ggplot2::element_text(size = 11),
    strip.text = ggplot2::element_text(size = 11, face = "bold")
  )
```

**Read together:** the all-donor and leave-one-out UMAPs ask the same question as the pseudobulk falsification — is **`ADRB2`** elevated across **SAVI**, or only when **`P6_STING_ht`** is included? Concordance between a muted **SAVI** panel after exclusion and the drop in SAVI mean **`log2fc`** in **`plot-adrb2-leave-one-out`** strengthens the **`falsified_no_savi_signal`** classification (20% of SAVI donors pass the strict atlas tail test).

# Composition analysis vs original SAVI paper

In the original SAVI scRNA-seq paper (de Cevins *et al.* 2023; GSE226598), after QC, integration, clustering, and annotation, the authors report **23 cell populations** in the SAVI dataset and **29 cell populations** in the IFN-beta dataset. They then compare PBMC composition between SAVI and controls (Figure 1E), with p-values from Kruskal-Wallis tests followed by post hoc Dunn's multiple-comparison testing.

For whole-PBMC composition, the paper reports increased naive CD4 and naive CD8 T cells, decreased effector/memory CD4 and CD8 T-cell compartments, decreased NK cells (especially NK CD56bright), and strong depletion of MAIT and gamma-delta T cells in SAVI. They also report that cell-type proportions did not differ significantly before versus under JAK-inhibitor treatment.

In this notebook, we use those statements as the reference conclusion, then:

1. compute per-sample proportions from GEO **`CellType`** (23 populations),
2. map **`CellType` → Immune Atlas `L3`** labels used by the sccomp composition model,
3. compare observed proportions to healthy **`predict_res`** draws matched on **`sex`** and **`age_decade`**,
4. summarise trends in **`CTRL`**, **`SAVI`**, and **`SAVI_treated`** against the paper’s Figure 1E conclusions.

```{r}
#| label: summarize-paper-composition
paper_composition_summary <- tibble::tribble(
  ~topic, ~paper_finding,
  "Dataset size after integration", "23 populations (SAVI dataset) and 29 populations (IFN-beta dataset).",
  "Naive T-cell compartments", "Naive CD4 and naive CD8 T-cell proportions are increased in SAVI.",
  "Effector/memory T-cell compartments", "Effector/memory CD4 and CD8 compartments are decreased in SAVI.",
  "Innate-like / cytotoxic compartments", "NK cells (notably NK CD56bright), MAIT cells, and gamma-delta T cells are reduced in SAVI.",
  "Treatment comparison", "No significant composition differences were observed before versus under JAK inhibitor treatment.",
  "Statistics in Figure 1E", "Kruskal-Wallis tests with post hoc Dunn's multiple comparisons."
)

paper_composition_summary

paper_ct_alignment <- tibble::tribble(
  ~paper_compartment, ~direction_in_savi, ~celltype_labels_in_this_object, ~mapping_note,
  "Naive CD4 T", "increased", "0. Naive CD4", "Directly aligned.",
  "Effector/memory CD4", "decreased", "3. CM CD4; 4. EM CD4; 8. TE CD4; 9. Tregs and TE CD4", "Approximate effector/memory CD4 pool from available labels.",
  "Naive CD8 T", "increased", "2. Naive CD8", "Directly aligned.",
  "Effector/memory CD8", "decreased", "14. CM CD8; 15. EM CD8; 7. TE CD8", "Approximate effector/memory CD8 pool from available labels.",
  "NK (especially CD56bright)", "decreased", "10. NK; 26. NK CD56bright", "CD56bright is explicitly available.",
  "MAIT", "strongly decreased", "22. MAIT", "Directly aligned.",
  "gamma-delta T", "strongly decreased", "16. gd T cells", "Directly aligned.",
  "Myeloid context (not primary Figure 1E claim)", "context", "5. Classical monocytes; 12. Non-classical monocytes; 17. Disease-associated monocytes; 20. cDCs; 27. pDCs", "Contextual comparison only.",
  "B-cell context (not primary Figure 1E claim)", "context", "1. Naive B; 6. Transitionnal B; 13. Memory B; 11. CD3+ B cells; 25. Plasmablasts", "Contextual comparison only."
)

paper_ct_alignment
```

```{r}
#| label: composition-proportions-build
#| cache: false

if (!exists("read_geo_rds_gz", mode = "function")) {
  read_geo_rds_gz <- function(path) {
    con <- gzcon(gzfile(path))
    on.exit(close(con), add = TRUE)
    readRDS(con)
  }
}

if (!exists("seurat_savi", inherits = FALSE)) {
  seurat_savi <- read_geo_rds_gz(params$savi_seurat_gz)
}

if (!"Category" %in% colnames(seurat_savi@meta.data)) {
  stop("`Category` not found in Seurat metadata.")
}
if (!"CellType" %in% colnames(seurat_savi@meta.data)) {
  stop("`CellType` not found in Seurat metadata.")
}

seurat_savi$Category <- factor(
  seurat_savi$Category,
  levels = c("CTRL", "SAVI", "SAVI_treated")
)

# GEO sample metadata (same table as pseudobulk join above).
geo_tbl_comp <- geo_tbl |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    sex = dplyr::case_when(
      .data$gse_sex == "M" ~ "male",
      .data$gse_sex == "F" ~ "female",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    age_decade = as.character(ceiling(.data$gse_age_years / 10))
  ) |>
  dplyr::select("Sample", "sex", "age_decade", "gse_age_years")

# Fine-grained CellType -> Immune Atlas L3 (posteriorHCA / sccomp) labels.
celltype_to_l3 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~cell_type, ~L3,
  "0. Naive CD4", "cd4 naive",
  "2. Naive CD8", "cd8 naive",
  "3. CM CD4", "cd4 tcm",
  "4. EM CD4", "cd4 th1 em",
  "8. TE CD4", "cd4 th1 em",
  "9. Tregs and TE CD4", "treg",
  "14. CM CD8", "cd8 tcm",
  "15. EM CD8", "cd8 tem",
  "7. TE CD8", "cd8 tem",
  "10. NK", "nk",
  "26. NK CD56bright", "nk",
  "22. MAIT", "mait",
  "16. gd T cells", "tgd",
  "1. Naive B", "b naive",
  "6. Transitionnal B", "b naive",
  "13. Memory B", "b memory",
  "11. CD3+ B cells", "b memory",
  "5. Classical monocytes", "cd14 mono",
  "12. Non-classical monocytes", "cd16 mono",
  "17. Disease-associated monocytes", "cd14 mono",
  "20. cDCs", "cdc",
  "27. pDCs", "pdc",
  "25. Plasmablasts", "plasma"
)

cell_tbl <- seurat_savi@meta.data |>
  tibble::rownames_to_column("cell_id") |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    sample_id = as.character(.data$Sample),
    Category = as.character(.data$Category),
    cell_type = as.character(.data$CellType)
  ) |>
  dplyr::left_join(celltype_to_l3, by = "cell_type") |>
  dplyr::left_join(geo_tbl_comp, by = c("sample_id" = "Sample"))

example_proportions_celltype <- cell_tbl |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(.data$cell_type), nzchar(.data$cell_type)) |>
  dplyr::count(.data$sample_id, .data$cell_type, name = "n_cells") |>
  dplyr::group_by(.data$sample_id) |>
  dplyr::mutate(proportion = .data$n_cells / sum(.data$n_cells)) |>
  dplyr::ungroup() |>
  dplyr::select(.data$sample_id, .data$cell_type, .data$proportion)

# L3-level observed proportions (merge CellType labels that map to the same L3).
example_proportions <- cell_tbl |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(.data$L3)) |>
  dplyr::count(.data$sample_id, .data$Category, .data$sex, .data$age_decade, .data$L3, name = "n_cells") |>
  dplyr::group_by(.data$sample_id, .data$Category, .data$sex, .data$age_decade, .data$L3) |>
  dplyr::summarise(proportion = sum(.data$n_cells), .groups = "drop_last") |>
  dplyr::group_by(.data$sample_id) |>
  dplyr::mutate(proportion = .data$proportion / sum(.data$proportion)) |>
  dplyr::ungroup() |>
  dplyr::rename(cell_type = L3) |>
  dplyr::arrange(.data$sample_id, .data$cell_type)

unmapped_celltypes <- cell_tbl |>
  dplyr::filter(is.na(.data$L3)) |>
  dplyr::count(.data$cell_type, sort = TRUE)

tibble::tibble(
  label_column_used = "CellType",
  n_samples = dplyr::n_distinct(example_proportions$sample_id),
  n_cells_total = nrow(cell_tbl),
  n_celltypes_raw = dplyr::n_distinct(example_proportions_celltype$cell_type),
  n_l3_types = dplyr::n_distinct(example_proportions$cell_type),
  n_unmapped_celltypes = nrow(unmapped_celltypes)
)

if (nrow(unmapped_celltypes) > 0L) {
  unmapped_celltypes
}
```

### Healthy atlas composition null (`predict_res`)

Posterior draws of blood PBMC composition from the Immune Atlas sccomp model (`disease_groups___altered = Normal`), stratified by **`sex`** (`male` / `female`) and **`age_decade`** (`1`–`4`), matching SAVI donor metadata. The draw table is **not** knitr-cached (too large for R’s cache serializer); it is saved once to **`params$composition_predict_rds`** and trimmed to L3 types present in the SAVI cohort.

```{r}
#| label: composition-predict-healthy
#| cache: false

if (!requireNamespace("sccomp", quietly = TRUE)) {
  stop("Package `sccomp` is required for composition prediction.")
}

l3_for_comparison <- example_proportions |>
  dplyr::distinct(.data$cell_type) |>
  dplyr::pull(.data$cell_type)

trim_predict_res <- function(x, cell_types) {
  x |>
    dplyr::filter(.data$cell_type %in% cell_types) |>
    dplyr::select(dplyr::any_of(c(
      "sample_id",
      "age_decade",
      "sex",
      "cell_type",
      "proportion",
      ".draw"
    )))
}

if (file.exists(params$composition_predict_rds)) {
  predict_res <- readRDS(params$composition_predict_rds)
} else {
  sccomp_est <- readRDS(params$sccomp_estimates_rds)

  sample_metadata <- tidyr::expand_grid(
    age_decade = as.character(1:4),
    sex = c("male", "female")
  ) |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      assay_groups___altered = "10x Genomics 3",
      disease_groups___altered = "Normal",
      tissue_groups = "blood",
      ethnicity_groups_imputed = NA,
      dataset_id___altered = NA,
      sample_id = paste0("S", dplyr::row_number())
    )

  predict_res <- sccomp_est |>
    sccomp::sccomp_predict(
      formula_composition = NULL,
      new_data = sample_metadata,
      summary_instead_of_draws = FALSE
    ) |>
    dplyr::rename(cell_type = L3) |>
    trim_predict_res(l3_for_comparison)

  predict_dir <- dirname(params$composition_predict_rds)
  if (!dir.exists(predict_dir)) {
    dir.create(predict_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
  }
  saveRDS(predict_res, params$composition_predict_rds, compress = "xz")
}

predict_res <- trim_predict_res(predict_res, l3_for_comparison)

predict_res |>
  dplyr::distinct(.data$age_decade, .data$sex, .data$cell_type) |>
  dplyr::count(.data$age_decade, .data$sex, name = "n_cell_types")
```

### Compare observed SAVI proportions to healthy predictive draws

For each donor we match **`predict_res`** rows with the same **`sex`** and **`age_decade`**, then compute empirical tail probabilities (same logic as `posteriorHCA::composition_posterior_test()`).

```{r}
#| label: composition-vs-healthy

composition_vs_healthy <- example_proportions |>
  dplyr::rename(
    sample_id_observed = sample_id,
    cell_type_observed = cell_type,
    proportion_observed = proportion
  ) |>
  dplyr::inner_join(
    predict_res |>
      dplyr::select(
        age_decade, sex, cell_type, proportion_sampled = proportion, .draw
      ),
    by = c("sex" = "sex", "age_decade" = "age_decade", "cell_type_observed" = "cell_type"),
    relationship = "many-to-many"
  ) |>
  dplyr::group_by(.data$sample_id_observed, .data$Category, .data$cell_type_observed) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    proportion_observed = dplyr::first(.data$proportion_observed),
    healthy_median = stats::median(.data$proportion_sampled),
    healthy_mean = mean(.data$proportion_sampled),
    healthy_hpd_lo = stats::quantile(.data$proportion_sampled, 0.025),
    healthy_hpd_hi = stats::quantile(.data$proportion_sampled, 0.975),
    # Same tail convention as `gene_deviation_from_fit()`: P(draw >= obs), not P(obs > draw).
    p_above_healthy = mean(.data$proportion_sampled >= .data$proportion_observed),
    p_below_healthy = mean(.data$proportion_sampled <= .data$proportion_observed),
    empirical_confidence = 2 * pmin(.data$p_above_healthy, .data$p_below_healthy),
    direction = dplyr::case_when(
      .data$p_above_healthy < 0.025 ~ "higher_than_healthy",
      .data$p_below_healthy < 0.025 ~ "lower_than_healthy",
      TRUE ~ "consistent_with_healthy"
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

composition_vs_healthy |>
  dplyr::arrange(.data$Category, .data$cell_type_observed, .data$sample_id_observed) |>
  dplyr::slice_head(n = 12)
```

### Paper compartments: trend by `Category` and comparison to published direction

We aggregate mapped L3 labels into the Figure 1E compartments from the paper, then summarise mean proportion per **`Category`** and compare the SAVI–CTRL direction to the published expectation.

```{r}
#| label: composition-paper-compartments

paper_compartment_l3 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~paper_compartment, ~direction_in_savi, ~cell_type,
  "Naive CD4 T", "increased", "cd4 naive",
  "Effector/memory CD4", "decreased", "cd4 tcm",
  "Effector/memory CD4", "decreased", "cd4 th1 em",
  "Effector/memory CD4", "decreased", "cd4 th17 em",
  "Effector/memory CD4", "decreased", "cd4 th2 em",
  "Effector/memory CD4", "decreased", "cd4 fh em",
  "Effector/memory CD4", "decreased", "cd4 th1/th17 em",
  "Effector/memory CD4", "decreased", "treg",
  "Naive CD8 T", "increased", "cd8 naive",
  "Effector/memory CD8", "decreased", "cd8 tcm",
  "Effector/memory CD8", "decreased", "cd8 tem",
  "NK", "decreased", "nk",
  "MAIT", "strongly decreased", "mait",
  "gamma-delta T", "strongly decreased", "tgd"
)

composition_paper_per_donor <- composition_vs_healthy |>
  dplyr::inner_join(paper_compartment_l3, by = c("cell_type_observed" = "cell_type")) |>
  dplyr::group_by(
    .data$sample_id_observed,
    .data$Category,
    .data$paper_compartment,
    .data$direction_in_savi
  ) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    proportion_observed = sum(.data$proportion_observed),
    healthy_median = sum(.data$healthy_median),
    direction = dplyr::if_else(
      any(.data$direction == "higher_than_healthy"),
      "higher_than_healthy",
      dplyr::if_else(
        any(.data$direction == "lower_than_healthy"),
        "lower_than_healthy",
        "consistent_with_healthy"
      )
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Donors with zero cells in a compartment are absent from counts; fill with 0 so
# category means (and CTRL dots) include all donors in each Category.
all_donors_comp <- example_proportions |>
  dplyr::distinct(.data$sample_id, .data$Category) |>
  dplyr::rename(sample_id_observed = sample_id)

compartment_meta <- paper_compartment_l3 |>
  dplyr::distinct(.data$paper_compartment, .data$direction_in_savi)

composition_paper_long <- tidyr::crossing(all_donors_comp, compartment_meta) |>
  dplyr::left_join(
    composition_paper_per_donor,
    by = c("sample_id_observed", "Category", "paper_compartment", "direction_in_savi")
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    proportion_observed = dplyr::coalesce(.data$proportion_observed, 0),
    healthy_median = dplyr::coalesce(.data$healthy_median, 0),
    direction = dplyr::coalesce(.data$direction, "consistent_with_healthy")
  )

composition_paper_summary <- composition_paper_long |>
  dplyr::group_by(.data$paper_compartment, .data$direction_in_savi, .data$Category) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    n_samples = dplyr::n(),
    mean_prop = mean(.data$proportion_observed),
    median_prop = stats::median(.data$proportion_observed),
    mean_healthy_median = mean(.data$healthy_median),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(
    names_from = Category,
    values_from = c(mean_prop, median_prop, n_samples),
    names_sep = "__"
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    delta_savi_minus_ctrl = .data$mean_prop__SAVI - .data$mean_prop__CTRL,
    delta_treated_minus_ctrl = .data$mean_prop__SAVI_treated - .data$mean_prop__CTRL,
    matches_paper_savi = dplyr::case_when(
      .data$direction_in_savi == "increased" ~ .data$delta_savi_minus_ctrl > 0,
      .data$direction_in_savi %in% c("decreased", "strongly decreased") ~ .data$delta_savi_minus_ctrl < 0,
      TRUE ~ NA
    ),
    matches_paper_treated = dplyr::case_when(
      .data$direction_in_savi == "increased" ~ .data$delta_treated_minus_ctrl > 0,
      .data$direction_in_savi %in% c("decreased", "strongly decreased") ~ .data$delta_treated_minus_ctrl < 0,
      TRUE ~ NA
    )
  ) |>
  dplyr::arrange(.data$paper_compartment)

composition_paper_summary
```

### Healthy baseline vs age decade

Healthy atlas predictive draws (`predict_res`, Normal blood): for each **paper compartment**, sum mapped L3 proportions per draw, then summarise by **`sex`** and **`age_decade`** (1–4).

```{r}
#| label: plot-composition-healthy-baseline-by-age
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 9
#| fig-align: center

healthy_baseline_compartment_age <- predict_res |>
  dplyr::inner_join(
    paper_compartment_l3 |>
      dplyr::distinct(.data$paper_compartment, .data$cell_type),
    by = "cell_type"
  ) |>
  dplyr::group_by(
    .data$paper_compartment,
    .data$sex,
    .data$age_decade,
    .data$.draw
  ) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    compartment_proportion = sum(.data$proportion),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  dplyr::group_by(
    .data$paper_compartment,
    .data$sex,
    .data$age_decade
  ) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    median_proportion = stats::median(.data$compartment_proportion),
    hpd_lo = stats::quantile(.data$compartment_proportion, 0.025),
    hpd_hi = stats::quantile(.data$compartment_proportion, 0.975),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    age_decade = factor(.data$age_decade, levels = as.character(1:4)),
    sex = factor(.data$sex, levels = c("female", "male")),
    paper_compartment = factor(
      .data$paper_compartment,
      levels = unique(paper_compartment_l3$paper_compartment)
    )
  )

sex_cols <- c(female = "#E41A1C", male = "#377EB8")

ggplot2::ggplot(
  healthy_baseline_compartment_age,
  ggplot2::aes(
    x = age_decade,
    y = median_proportion,
    color = sex,
    group = sex
  )
) +
  ggplot2::geom_ribbon(
    ggplot2::aes(ymin = hpd_lo, ymax = hpd_hi, fill = sex),
    alpha = 0.15,
    color = NA
  ) +
  ggplot2::geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) +
  ggplot2::geom_point(size = 2.2) +
  ggplot2::facet_wrap(~paper_compartment, scales = "free_y", ncol = 2) +
  ggplot2::scale_color_manual(values = sex_cols, name = "Sex") +
  ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(values = sex_cols, guide = "none") +
  ggplot2::labs(
    title = "Healthy atlas compartment proportion by sex and age decade",
    subtitle = paste(
      "Lines = posterior median per decade; ribbon = 2.5–97.5% across predictive draws.",
      "Compartment mass = sum of mapped L3 proportions (sccomp Normal blood)."
    ),
    x = "Age decade",
    y = "Compartment proportion (healthy baseline)"
  ) +
  ggplot2::theme_bw() +
  ggplot2::theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    strip.text = ggplot2::element_text(face = "bold", size = 9)
  )
```

### Observed composition (within cohort)

Boxplot and bar chart use **observed** compartment proportions only (CTRL / SAVI / SAVI_treated); no healthy atlas reference.

```{r}

category_cols <- c(
```
